name: TestDiagSuite/TestDiagOutput
statusMessage:
timed out after 5m0.000306269s (excluding download) waiting for app "24d773e8-c752-4ab9-a84f-f2817cc37881" (diag-reader) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: CREATING_VOLUME)

Claude's conclusion:
Confirmed: the `extract-*` snapshot is still `Active` (uncommitted) for the diag-reader image layer — exactly the unpack-stall signature. I have enough evidence now.

**Root cause:** `diag-reader`'s volume (`9ebd7ba3-ba11-49ea-9ec3-328d02fc7581`) entered `CREATING_VOLUME` and is still there live — `ctr snapshots ls` shows an `extract-601665617-P_cQ` snapshot still `Active` (uncommitted) for the image layer. Live `nproc`/`vmstat` on `edge-dev` show the classic CPU/IO-oversubscription signature seen repeatedly in this ledger: the guest reports only `nproc=1` against a device configured for 4 vCPUs, and `vmstat` shows a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1`, `wa`≈24-26%). This is corroborated by `evetest broker status`: host `farfalle` is running 13/16 VMs at 102% of host RAM assigned with 1.9 GiB swap in use — the same oversubscription condition that has slowed image unpacks past the fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`→`RUNNING` budget throughout this ledger.

This is a **known, recurring issue**: `TestDiagOutput` (same test, same app `diag-reader`) failed with this identical `CREATING_VOLUME` timeout signature back on 2026-11-20 (run #30), where the conclusion then was also CPU-oversubscription-driven slow volume casting (that time it did eventually complete at 7m44s). It also matches the broader, heavily-recurring `CREATING_VOLUME`/unpack-stall-under-host-CPU-oversubscription class that has hit dozens of different tests/suites in nearly every nightly run since at least 2026-11-20 — an infrastructure/environment issue, not a product regression. No PR diff was supplied for this investigation, so no relatedness judgment is given.

### Root cause

The volume didn't actually get stuck — the live device now shows `VolumeStatus` for `b69b1f63-7369-4b8a-8d58-29f25837fabf` at `State:110 (CREATED_VOLUME)`, `CreateTime:"2026-11-20T17:07:42Z"`, and `app-info` shows the app progressed all the way to `RUNNING`. So volume creation (casting the 56MB encrypted container image into `/persist/vault/...`) simply took from 16:59:58 to 17:07:42 — about 7m44s — well past the test's 5-minute timeout, and then completed successfully with no error ever recorded (`Error:""` throughout).

This points to resource starvation on the runner host rather than a pillar bug: `nproc` on this host is only 2, yet the EVE device alone is configured for 4 vCPUs/8GiB (`evetest status` shows `CPUs: 4, Memory: 8.00 GiB`), and at the time of the test it was sharing those 2 physical cores with the evetest orchestrator, `go test`, the Adam controller, and Docker/containerd (all visible in `ps aux` right now). This kind of CPU oversubscription is known to make vault/LUKS-encrypted volume casting (CPU-heavy crypto + image conversion) unpredictably slow. I checked the recent `volumemgr` worker-pool-refusal fix (`099aad80f`, already present on this branch) which addresses a different bug (a *refused* submission silently wedging the volume forever, state `Preparing`); this device's `SubState` was `PrepareDone` (work was accepted, just slow to finish), so that fix doesn't apply here and there's no sign of the bug it addresses.

I found no ledger file in the accessible directories to check for recurring occurrences, and this run has no earlier failure to compare against. No PR diff was provided for this investigation.
